extracted.intended_audience: clinicians and other authors preparing medical case reports (researchers, educators, journal authors/editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for clinicians and researchers on preparing accurate, transparent, and useful medical case reports using the CARE guidelines; includes guidance for organizing, formatting, and submitting case reports or preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, transparency, and usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The CARE guidelines were developed by an international group of experts to support an increase in the accuracy, transparency, and usefulness of case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines have been endorsed by multiple medical journals and publishers and translated into multiple languages; authors are encouraged to follow the CARE checklist and guidance to achieve these goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear focus (importance in context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good case reporting demands a clear focus, to make explicit to the audience why a particular observation is important in the context of existing knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should make explicit why their observation matters relative to current evidence or practice (Vandenbroucke 2001). A clear focus helps readers understand the relevance of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce risk of bias
rubrics_metrics.description: The CARE guidelines help authors reduce risk of bias in case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured, transparent reporting (per the checklist/manual) to minimize selective reporting and other biases that can mislead readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide early signals of effectiveness/appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Case reports following the CARE guidelines provide early signals of what works, for which patients, and under which circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-documented cases can generate hypotheses and early indications of interventions' effects; authors should report contextual details to clarify applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support measurement of clinician- and patient-assessed outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Case reports should support measurement of clinician- and patient-assessed outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include outcome measures (clinician-reported and patient-reported) where relevant, reported transparently so readers can assess change and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support measurement of effectiveness of Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case reports can inform assessment of the effectiveness of Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether guideline-recommended care was followed and the observed outcomes to contribute evidence about guideline performance in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support measurement of return on investment (ROI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case reports can support assessment of return on investment (ROI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on resource use, costs, or downstream effects where applicable to help stakeholders evaluate value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the CARE checklist / guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are instructed to view and use the CARE checklist and accompanying manual when preparing case reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CARE checklist and manuals (published 2013 and 2017) provide the specific items and explanations; the checklist is downloadable and the guideline has been endorsed by journals and integrated with the EQUATOR Network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and format case reports systematically and transparently (use CARE-writer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use tools and a structured approach to organize, format and write systematic and transparent case reports and case report preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CARE-writer is an online application that helps authors follow the CARE guidelines to prepare case reports for posting on preprint servers or submission to scientific journals; authors should format reports to meet journal or preprint server requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make reports useful to multiple stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Case reports should be prepared to benefit healthcare stakeholder groups including patients, clinicians, researchers, educators, authors, and medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor reporting so that: patients can review/compare options; clinicians can engage in peer-to-peer communication; researchers can develop hypotheses; educators can use cases for learning; authors can simplify writing; journals can use CARE-guided reports for peer review and author guidelines.
